channel.title: Quant Arena
channel.description: Weekly arena reports, research articles and site updates.

item.title: We Backtested 72 Strategies. After Adjusting for Luck, None Clearly Beat the Odds.
item.description: 104 strategy-and-market combinations look statistically convincing on their own. Once you account for the fact that we tested hundreds of them at the same time, the number drops to zero. Here is what that means for reading any leaderboard, including ours.

item.title: We Tried to Backtest 1,063 Free MT5 Expert Advisors. Here Is What Survived.
item.description: Free MetaTrader 5 EAs from the MQL5 CodeBase, converted automatically and tested on four markets for one year. More than half could not be converted at all. Of the 1,421 results we trust, about half made money — but on currencies the typical EA ended flat, only 40 EAs were profitable on all four markets, and one in five gold runs wiped out the account.

item.title: Which Trading Strategies Survived 2022? 62 Backtests Through Three Sell-offs
item.description: In the 2022 bear market SPY fell 24.5% from peak to trough. Every one of the 62 strategies we run on SPY lost less, and ten of them made money. Mean reversion held up best, momentum worst. Here is what the COVID crash and the late-2018 sell-off add to the picture.

item.title: Why Martingale and Grid EAs Blow Up: What 1,515 Free MT5 Expert Advisors and Their Losing Streaks Show
item.description: Martingale and grid EAs make up 5% of the free MT5 Expert Advisors we review, but more than half of the ones we rate "dangerous". The reason is arithmetic: losing streaks of six to eight trades are normal — and that is exactly where doubling the position runs out of money.

item.title: Do Moving-Average Strategies Still Work on Bitcoin? Nine Systems, Five Years
item.description: Over the last five years buy-and-hold bitcoin returned 7.2% a year with a 77% drawdown. Five of nine moving-average-style systems beat that return, and every one of them cut the worst drawdown. Over the full history the picture flips: almost nothing beats simply holding.

item.title: Does Turtle Trading Still Work? Ten Markets, 2021–2026
item.description: Two breakout systems, ten markets, five years. Neither beat buy-and-hold on most markets, but the slower Donchian version had a smaller drawdown on nine of ten, and both made money on commodities in the 2022 bear market when stocks fell 25%.

item.title: Does an RSI Filter Make MACD Better? A Ten-Market Test
item.description: Adding an RSI filter to a MACD crossover cut the maximum drawdown on nine of ten markets and reduced trading by 10–30%. It improved the Sharpe ratio on only five, and gave up return on the strongest trends — silver, bitcoin and ether.

item.title: Two Strategies, the Same 10% Drawdown, Very Different Pain: How to Read Drawdown, the Ulcer Index and Rolling Sharpe
item.description: Maximum drawdown tells you how deep the worst fall was, not how long you spent underwater or how often it happened. Two strategies on the S&P 500 with almost identical 10% drawdowns show why the Ulcer index and drawdown duration are worth a look — and why a single Sharpe ratio can mislead as much as a single drawdown.

item.title: Keltner Breakout or Bollinger Reversion? Ten Markets Split Down the Middle
item.description: Two volatility-band strategies that do opposite things: one buys when price breaks out of a Keltner Channel, the other buys when price falls to the lower Bollinger Band. Over the last five years each had the better Sharpe ratio on exactly five of ten markets — and the split follows a clear pattern: breakouts won where prices trended, reversion won where they went back and forth.

item.title: Eight new research articles
item.description: New data-driven articles on luck-adjusted Sharpe ratios across 72 strategies, which strategies held up in 2022, 1,063 free MT5 EAs backtested, why martingale and grid EAs blow up, moving averages on bitcoin, turtle trading since 2021, MACD with an RSI filter, and how to read drawdown, the Ulcer index and rolling Sharpe. The Keltner vs Bollinger article was rewritten with ten-market results.

item.title: Browse Expert Advisors by category
item.description: Each EA category — trend following, grid, martingale, scalping and more — now has its own page with a short explanation, backtest statistics for the whole group, how many EAs are rated dangerous, and every EA sorted by how many markets it made money on.

item.title: EA backtests rerun with realistic position sizes
item.description: The converted EAs kept adding orders while one was still pending and treated lots as units, so positions grew far beyond the EA's lot size and most P&L figures were wrong. All 1,063 EAs were rerun on four markets with MT5 lot sizes, 1:100 leverage, one order at a time and a broker-style stop-out. Three conversion bugs that kept some EAs from ever trading were fixed. The EA Ranking now also shows the recovery factor and on how many markets each EA made money. Results that rely on a placeholder for a custom indicator are now labeled as approximations and left out of the ranking, and EA pages explain why an EA never traded when the cause is a conversion bug.

item.title: Confidence ranges for every strategy
item.description: Strategy pages show a 90% bootstrap range for CAGR and maximum drawdown, plus the chance of a loss, so you can see how much a result depends on a few lucky stretches. A new glossary entry explains how it is computed.

item.title: Clearer EA backtest status and a trading-cost slider
item.description: EA backtests now say why a result is missing: the EA could not be converted automatically (most cases), it held one position to the end, or it really never traded. Strategy pages have a slider that shows the annual return after 0–50 bp of trading costs.

item.title: Shareable portfolios and quick links to new tools
item.description: Portfolio weights in the compare view now live in the link, so a mix of strategies can be bookmarked or shared with one click. The home page links straight to the Strategy Lab, today's signals, the heatmap, weekly reports and the glossary.

item.title: Strategy Lab: compare your own backtest
item.description: Upload an equity curve (CSV) or a MetaTrader strategy tester report and see where it ranks against every arena strategy on the same market and the same trading days. Everything is computed in your browser; nothing is uploaded.

item.title: Crisis tests, luck-adjusted Sharpe and embeddable badges
item.description: Strategy pages now show how each strategy did in the Q4 2018 sell-off, the COVID crash and the 2022 bear market, its returns above and below the 200-day average, CAGR after 10 bp trading costs, and the Deflated Sharpe Ratio, which corrects for testing many strategies at once. Each strategy also has a live Arena Score badge you can embed.

item.title: Chinese strategy pages and share images
item.description: All 72 strategy pages and the category pages now have Chinese versions, and every strategy has a share image with its equity curve and key numbers for social media previews.

item.title: Today's signals, strategy heatmap, weekly reports and RSS
item.description: New pages show the current position of every strategy on every market, an Arena Score heatmap of strategies × markets, and an automatic weekly report (market moves, signal changes, best and worst strategies). Follow along with the RSS feed at /feed.xml (Chinese: /zh/feed.xml).

item.title: Arena Score v2 and 20 new metrics
item.description: The Arena Score now ranks each strategy against the others on the same market and window across five components (return quality, drawdown control, consistency, robustness, significance), so the leaderboard no longer has blocks of ties at 100 or 0, and strategies that were almost never in the market are not ranked. Strategy pages add time in market, Ulcer index, longest drawdown, VaR/CVaR, alpha, beta, capture ratios and the probabilistic Sharpe ratio, with five new glossary entries.

item.title: Every strategy, article and EA now has its own page
item.description: 72 strategy pages with equity curves, results on every market and a buy-and-hold comparison; strategy category hubs; research articles in English and Chinese; a 12-term metrics glossary with live examples; and 1,515 EA pages in both languages. Pages load fast and can be found by search engines.

item.title: EA rankings now only use reliable backtests
item.description: Sharpe ratios are recomputed from each equity curve (the old values used yearly returns and were often meaningless). Results with no trades, run errors or flat curves are labelled and left out of the ranking, and detail pages say why.

item.title: Site-wide search and recently viewed
item.description: Press / or Ctrl/Cmd+K anywhere to search strategies, EAs, research notes and pages. The home page now remembers what you opened recently (stored only in your browser).

item.title: Redesigned header, home page and footer
item.description: A cleaner navigation with a More menu, icon theme and language toggles, a new home overview with live counts, quick-entry cards, ranked top strategies, a timeline changelog, back-to-top button and a reading progress bar on articles.

item.description: What moved in the arena during the week ending 2026-11-02: market moves, strategies that changed position, and the best and worst performers over the last month.

item.title: Donchian Channel and Turtle Breakout: Trading the 20/10 Rule
item.description: The Turtle system uses Donchian breakouts and risk based sizing to capture sustained trends. This research note explains the logic, market fit, and failure modes.

item.title: Supertrend and ATR Trailing Stop: Volatility Adjusted Trend Control
item.description: Supertrend uses ATR based bands to define trend flips and stops. This research note explains the signal mechanics, regime fit, and the risks of whipsaw.

item.title: Ichimoku Cloud Strategy: Regime, Momentum, and Support in One System
item.description: Ichimoku combines trend, momentum, and support into a single framework. This research note breaks down the components, signals, and common traps.

item.title: RSI Mean Reversion Strategy: Buying Weakness Inside Ranges
item.description: RSI mean reversion looks for short term exhaustion and then fades the move. This research note covers the signal logic, market fit, and risk traps.

item.title: EMA Crossover Strategy: Reading Trend With Two Clocks
item.description: An in depth look at why exponential moving average crossovers persist, how to interpret their backtests, and when trend signals fail.

item.title: Parabolic SAR Strategy: A Trend Exit Engine
item.description: Parabolic SAR uses a trailing stop that accelerates with trend strength. This article explains why it works, when it fails, and how to read its backtests.

item.title: Volatility Breakout Strategy: Trading Expansion Without Overreach
item.description: Volatility breakouts focus on price moves that escape a recent range. This guide explains the logic, the regimes where it works, and the traps to avoid.

item.title: How QuantArenas Ranks Strategies
item.description: A full methodology essay on why the Arena Score blends multiple metrics, how stability is measured, and how to read results without overfitting.
